findings.title: Post-validation bookkeeping is meaningless for federated recovery-code credentials
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now prefers the credential returned by the user storage's `getCredentials()`. For such a credential the `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` is built by the provider (in the test provider via `createFromValues`, so it has no id and all codes are always unused). The authenticator then calls `allCodesUsed()` on it, which can never be true, and if it ever were, `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` would target the local DB (with a possibly null id, which `em.find` rejects) rather than the user storage. Consequently a user whose codes live in user storage is never forced to `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` when codes run out, and the 'remove exhausted credential' logic silently does nothing. The federated branch needs its own semantics (delegate consumption/removal to the storage) or this code path should be restricted to locally stored credentials.

findings.title: Test storage never consumes recovery codes and the test doesn't check code consumption or the displayed code number
findings.body: `isValid` for recovery codes only checks `anyMatch` against the stored raw list and never marks a code as used, and `getCredentials` rebuilds the model with `createFromValues`, so `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` is always code 0. The new `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` therefore only logs in once with code 0 and cannot detect regressions where codes are not consumed, where a second login is asked for the wrong code number, or where an invalid/reused code is accepted. At minimum the test should attempt a second login (expecting a different code number / rejection of the reused code) and a login with a wrong code, with the test provider tracking used codes.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences possibly-null MyUser
findings.body: `getCredentials` calls `getMyUser(user)` and immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` / `myUser.otp` without a null check, unlike `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` which all guard against `myUser == null`. If the user was removed from the in-memory map while a cached/federated `UserModel` still exists (e.g. during cleanup or `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` calls from other tests), this throws a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream.

findings.title: Backwards-compatibility provider now uses APIs that did not exist in the version it claims to represent
findings.body: The class Javadoc states this provider was written against Keycloak 4.8.3 and must keep compiling unchanged to prove compatibility. This PR adds an override of `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials(...)` and support for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, neither of which existed in 4.8.3, so the provider no longer demonstrates what its documentation says. Either update the Javadoc to reflect the new mixed purpose or put the recovery-code support into a separate test storage provider so the backwards-compatibility guarantee is still meaningfully exercised.

findings.title: Raw (unhashed) recovery codes are handed to arbitrary user storage providers without documenting it
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializes the plaintext generated codes into the `UserCredentialModel` challenge response and passes it to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`, i.e. to any `CredentialInputUpdater` that claims to support the `recovery-authn-codes` type. The local path stores only hashes. Any existing third-party storage provider that returns true from `supportsCredentialType` for this type (or generically) will now receive plaintext recovery codes, which is a behavior change not called out in the Javadoc or the PR. The method's Javadoc should state that the raw codes are delivered to the storage and that the storage is responsible for hashing/consuming them.
